overall_quality.evidence: Eventual consistency is a model in distributed computing where data stored in multiple nodes or servers is updated asynchronously. This means that updates to the data may not be immediately visible to all nodes, and there can be a delay before all nodes reflect the latest changes. The term "eventual" refers to the fact that the system will eventually reach a state where all nodes have the same data, but this may take some time. This model is often used in distributed databases and other systems where data is replicated across multiple nodes to ensure availability and fault tolerance.
